evidence_entries.statement: INAH locates four serpent-head carvings beside the Etapa IVb stairs, with traces of original coloring; its visitor text identifies the Coyolxauhqui object at the stair foot as a COPY.
evidence_entries.exact_locator: Punto 1. Etapa IVb. Gobierno de Axayácatl (1469–1481): Cabeza de serpiente and La Coyolxauhqui al pie de la escalinata
evidence_entries.access_scope: institutional HTML passage examined; excavation publication and object conservation record not independently examined
evidence_entries.educational_use: Ask visitors to compare the polychrome serpent heads and the replica; do not present the replica as the original monolith
evidence_entries.remaining_gap: verify on-site display placement and color preservation from museum conservation report

evidence_entries.statement: INAH identifies a brick water-collector duct underneath the metal walkway; says its construction cut about two metres through all temple building phases and passes under Guatemala street.
evidence_entries.exact_locator: Etapa IV y V > Colector de agua
evidence_entries.access_scope: INAH institutional HTML section examined; original 1900 engineering plan unexamined
evidence_entries.educational_use: Point out red-brick duct below walkway as direct evidence of modern infrastructure severing older construction
evidence_entries.remaining_gap: inspect engineering plans, stratigraphy and exact construction date

evidence_entries.statement: INAH dates discovery of Coyolxauhqui sculpture by Compañía de Luz y Fuerza workers to 21 February 1978; Salvamento Arqueológico subsequently excavated the monument and the original museum plan evolved into Proyecto Templo Mayor.
evidence_entries.access_scope: INAH project-history HTML examined; original discovery field notes and photographs not inspected
evidence_entries.educational_use: Distinguish accidental utility-work discovery, rescue excavation and subsequent planned project; 1914 Gamio investigations predate it
